items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1960-03-15
items.q: I played over there with Sharky on the truck

ctx.x: The colored men were on the white union. Bob Kay and those fellas. Well, you all used to play nine unions.

We had permission from the union to get out of that man. Oh, that Johnny Pijos. He's a livin'. He's living? Sure. How old is he? What did you mean him, Bill? Charlie Patsutzi from Bloxy? No? No. He must be these men. Oh, he can't be living. Yes, it is. I'm back to 1900 years old. I played over there with Sharky on the truck and he rode the old thing around us. Where did he get permission to see? To get outside men. You know anybody called that, Bloxy? Yes, I don't know. I hate Tutszi J.
Yeah. So they gave you permission, huh?

items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1958-09-24
items.q: Schalke didn't even know how to hold on. He just knew how to pick up the numbers, you know, with his left hand, you know. Yeah. I said, well, I'll try to play, you know, with your right hand.

ctx.x: What year was it you quit?

I quit in 28. See? 1928. And never played a job since. I just wanted to show you, many of the times, Santa, years back, he wanted me to say, go ahead, write this up. He said, no, of course I've got my grades and everything. I can't do it. I said, Santa, I don't want to have nothing to do with that. I'm too old for that. You know what I mean? I just. But I always got in contact with all the musicians. It was like Paul Morez, Leon Rapport, Georgia Brunis. Always, always in contact. Leon's dead. Paul's dead. You…

Well, I was wondering, speaking of names, like your father's name, what is your full name? We might be nice to have it here on the record. My full name? Johnny Lowe. And the middle name? I had it. N is my middle name, but I never used it. In case there would be any confusion, I thought it would be good to have it in the middle. Yeah, Johnny Lowe.
